doc.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015

title: Pop songs on Bridging the Gap and big ears
summary: Overjoyed and One Less Bell choices and the importance of listening for rhythm section players.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Yeah, I love it. You know and so that “Bridging the Gap” record had a rock influence — more pop, not rock but pop influence. Stevie Wonder “Overjoyed” was just one of my favorite songs and Rossano tackled it and did a great job on it.

Then we did a Fifth Dimension song. “One Less Bell [to Answer]” I said Nicki, can you sing this?” She said, “it’s funny, my teacher just mentioned this song to me.” I said, “great.” She says, “okay, we’ll do it.” And there it is.
Well you have big ears. Not literally, but you know what I mean.

Yeah. I think it’s really important, especially for rhythm section guys. You know you’re playing in a trumpet section or an orchestra you have to listen to what’s going on. You have to listen to your section leader. You’ve got to match their pitch, whether it’s right or wrong. You’ve got to match their pitch. You’ve got to follow the conductor. It’s pretty simple when you think about it. Some guys make it too complicated.
